declared_purpose: Publish websites and files to live URLs, with personal or workspace ownership and access controls; also provide private Drive storage and scoped sharing. Supporting workflows include authentication, updates, version recovery, and account management (SKILL.md:4–16,23–29,114–188). Documentation checks, platform attribution, and saving received API keys are explicit instructions; recursive file selection, cache retention, and sharing defaults are helper implementation choices.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve service documentation
data_operations.data_scope: Current documentation and, when needed, API schemas; no instruction to attach user files or conversation content.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://here.now/docs and https://here.now/openapi.json
data_operations.condition: First related interaction, capability or workflow questions, and specified management tasks. Failed retrieval permits using local source and API output.

data_operations.operation: Collect sign-in information and request an API key
data_operations.source: User-provided email address and one-time sign-in code
data_operations.data_scope: Email sent to request-code; email and code sent to verify-code; returned apiKey received by the caller.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Agent conversation; https://here.now/api/auth/agent/request-code and /api/auth/agent/verify-code
data_operations.condition: Documented upgrade from anonymous to permanent publishing; not required for anonymous publishing.

data_operations.operation: Persist a received account credential
data_operations.source: Agent following the explicit credential-saving instruction
data_operations.data_scope: Account API key
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.herenow/credentials, with chmod 600 in the documented command
data_operations.condition: Immediately after receiving an API key. This is an entry-document requirement; neither helper implements this write.

data_operations.operation: Read credentials locally and construct authorization
data_operations.source: Both helpers: flags, HERENOW_API_KEY, HERENOW_DRIVE_TOKEN, and the credentials file
data_operations.data_scope: Account API key or scoped Drive token; credential-file whitespace is removed. Drive tokens take authorization precedence over account keys.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Helper process memory; bearer headers on subsequent API requests
data_operations.condition: Publishing permits anonymous operation. Drive commands require credentials. Non-default API bases require an explicit override before credentials are sent.

data_operations.operation: Read local files and derive upload metadata
data_operations.source: publish.sh local-file path; drive.sh put/import paths
data_operations.data_scope: File names, relative paths, sizes, MIME types, SHA-256 hashes, and file bytes read for hashing. Publishing recursively includes regular files except named exclusions; Drive import has a different exclusion set.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local helper processes and in-memory manifests
data_operations.condition: Selected local file or directory. Publishing excludes root .herenow/state.json and fork-meta.json; Drive import excludes root .git and node_modules trees and .DS_Store files.

data_operations.operation: Create or update a publication
data_operations.data_scope: Relative file paths, sizes, MIME types and hashes; optional viewer text, TTL, claimToken, folder, routing settings and baseVersionId. Headers carry an available API key, normalized client attribution, and optional workspace selector.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured BASE_URL/api/v1/publish or /api/v1/publish/{slug}; default https://here.now
data_operations.condition: Every local publication. Existing slugs use PUT; new Sites use POST. Platform attribution is explicitly requested by SKILL.md; optional instance names are also supported.

data_operations.operation: Upload file bytes directly to returned storage targets
data_operations.source: publish.sh upload loop and drive.sh put_file
data_operations.data_scope: Selected file bytes and Content-Type; these PUT requests do not attach the account bearer header.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: API-returned upload URLs, documented as *.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
data_operations.condition: Publishing uploads only response-listed files and skips files the service identifies as unchanged. Drive put uploads the selected file after creating an upload session.

data_operations.operation: Finalize a local publication
data_operations.data_scope: versionId, available account bearer credential, client attribution, and optional workspace selector
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The response-provided upload.finalizeUrl
data_operations.condition: After all requested uploads succeed, including when unchanged files require no upload. This required action makes the Site live; the returned URL's origin is not validated in the helper.

data_operations.operation: Request publication of a Drive snapshot
data_operations.data_scope: Drive ID, optional snapshot version, target slug, viewer text, folder and routing settings; account bearer credential and client attribution
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured BASE_URL/api/v1/publish/from-drive; resulting Site managed by here.now
data_operations.condition: Explicit --from-drive selection; requires an account key and rejects a local target or workspace. The documented version default is current head. Exact server-side file selection is unavailable.

data_operations.operation: Retain and serve published content and versions
data_operations.data_scope: Published files and immutable publication versions
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: here.now-managed Sites and visitors permitted by the Site's access mode; workspace Sites belong to the team
data_operations.condition: Finalized publication. Personal default access is anyone_with_link; workspace default is member-only. Anonymous Sites expire after 24 hours; authenticated Sites are described as permanent, with optional TTL support. Byte-identical republishes do not create a new version.

data_operations.operation: Read and persist local publication state
data_operations.data_scope: Slug, Site URL, live version ID, absolute source path, and returned claimToken, token-bearing claimUrl and expiresAt. Existing fields survive merges.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: .herenow/state.json in the working directory
data_operations.condition: Claim tokens may be loaded for updates; base versions are reused only for the same slug and absolute source path. Successful local publications save state, including authenticated republishes. The Drive-publication branch exits before this write.

data_operations.operation: Return publication results to the caller and direct user-facing reporting
data_operations.data_scope: Site and workspace URLs, claim URL when returned, slug, version IDs, folder, authentication mode, credential source category, expiry and warnings
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Helper caller; entry document directs sharing relevant URLs and status with the user
data_operations.condition: Successful publication. A claim URL must start with https:// before the helper reports it. These returns do not independently establish disclosure to another service or log retention.

data_operations.operation: Create Drives and read Drive metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Drive name and default flag on creation; Drive IDs, names, head versions, file paths and metadata on reads
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured BASE_URL/api/v1/drives endpoints; results remain with the caller or helper
data_operations.condition: Requested commands or prerequisite name resolution. An explicit drv_ ID avoids name lookup; a custom name requires fetching the Drive list. Scoped tokens cannot resolve names.

data_operations.operation: Write files into private Drive storage
data_operations.data_scope: Destination path, size, MIME type, SHA-256 and existing ETag or ifNoneMatch; file bytes through the upload target; uploadId on finalize
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured Drive uploads/finalize API and returned storage URL; selected Drive
data_operations.condition: Files at most 500 MiB. Writes preserve concurrency conditions. Import applies this per selected file; import --dry-run reads local paths and sizes and reports plans without invoking put_file.

data_operations.operation: Read Drive file content and optionally persist it locally
data_operations.data_scope: Requested file bytes, or paginated file paths and bytes matching an export prefix
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Authenticated reads from configured Drive API; cat returns bytes to caller, export writes under the specified local destination
data_operations.condition: Requested cat/export. Export --dry-run still performs remote metadata listing but skips content downloads and local file writes.

data_operations.operation: Create and return a Drive-sharing capability
data_operations.data_scope: Permissions, optional pathPrefix, TTL, label and manageTokens; returned token-bearing shareBlock
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured /api/v1/drives/{id}/tokens endpoint; shareBlock returns to the caller. A subsequent intended handoff gives it to another agent.
data_operations.condition: Explicit share command. Helper defaults are write permission, no prefix and no TTL field; the document says a null prefix means full-Drive access and recommends a narrow prefix and short TTL. Handoff instructions use the block's api_base.

data_operations.operation: Request deletion or capability revocation
data_operations.data_scope: File path and ETag for single-file deletion; prefix and head version for recursive deletion; token ID for revocation; Drive ID for Drive deletion
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured Drive API
data_operations.condition: Requested command. Recursive file deletion requires matching path confirmation; Drive deletion requires matching Drive-name confirmation. Responses establish API requests, not physical erasure or historical-version purging.

data_operations.operation: Temporarily persist API response bodies and delete temporary copies
data_operations.data_scope: Complete API response bodies, potentially including Drive metadata and generated sharing credentials; errors are returned to the caller
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local mktemp file, then caller/process memory
data_operations.condition: Calls routed through api_json. The helper removes the temporary file after success and handled HTTP errors; no interruption cleanup trap is shown.

data_operations.operation: Read owned Site content and manage version recovery
data_operations.source: Agent following update and drift instructions
data_operations.data_scope: Current version ID, source and creation time; live file lists and file bytes; publication history and selected restore version
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Authenticated here.now owner endpoints; caller and local files when reconciling
data_operations.condition: Drift checks before editing an authenticated Site not touched recently, conflict reconciliation, or requested history/rollback. Owner reads require an API key rather than a visitor password.

data_operations.operation: Manage access and account-facing metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Site allowlisted emails/domains, access mode and password; requested folder names, profile visibility or vanity subdomain. Vanity Site addresses are described as derived from titles.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: here.now access, metadata, folder, profile and vanity services; permitted visitors or public-profile viewers as configured
data_operations.condition: Relevant requested workflow. Access allowlists are read, merged and replaced; folders must be user-requested. Several complete schemas are deferred to unavailable current documentation.

potential_excess.data_scope: Incidental non-site files inside a publication directory, potentially including credential files, repository history or nested .herenow/state.json files
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Publication API receives their manifest metadata; returned storage targets receive requested bytes; Site visitors may receive published content under the configured access mode.
potential_excess.condition: A selected directory contains artifacts outside the intended website or shared-file set. Recursion filters only the named exclusions, including state exclusion at the root-relative path.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Publishing intended website assets and selected files; the document's directory-root model does not establish that incidental local artifacts are needed.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Enumerate and upload the complete intended publication, including deliberately required hidden configuration.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Publish a prepared output directory or explicit inclusion set; exclude incidental credentials, repository data and nested local state.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain every intended asset and required .herenow/proxy.json configuration. This narrows data within required publish actions rather than removing those actions.

potential_excess.data_scope: Incidental local credentials, token-bearing .herenow/state.json, or nested repository/dependency files selected by Drive import
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Drive upload metadata API, returned storage URL, and the selected private Drive
potential_excess.condition: The imported folder contains these files and the requested storage task does not include archiving them. Import has no .herenow/state.json exclusion and only root-relative .git/node_modules exclusions.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Persist the user's intended agent files privately; privacy of the destination does not make unrelated credentials necessary.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Import all files actually selected for the storage task.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Support explicit inclusions and configurable exclusions for local state, credentials and incidental trees.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Allow deliberate backups of those files when requested; retain the existing path mapping, size limit and concurrency checks.

potential_excess.data_scope: Optional agent instance, persona or bot name appended to the platform identifier
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: X-HereNow-Client header on publication create/update, finalize and from-drive requests
potential_excess.condition: The caller uses the optional platform/instance form; normalization retains the identifying text.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The explicit attribution requirement is to identify the agent product or harness. Instance identity is optional.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use only the platform name unless instance-level attribution is specifically needed.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the platform identifier and publish-sh attribution. This removes extra header data from required requests.

potential_excess.data_scope: Cached anonymous claimToken accompanying an authenticated update
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Configured BASE_URL/api/v1/publish/{slug}, in the update JSON body
potential_excess.condition: A slug has a cached claim token and an account API key is available. Auto-loading and body insertion do not test whether the update is authenticated.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Authorize and update the Site. The source comment states that the server uses claim tokens only for anonymous Sites.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Send the account bearer credential for authenticated updates; send a claim token when an anonymous update needs it.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Gate automatic claim-token loading and transmission on anonymous authentication mode.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve claim-token support for anonymous updates and retain any still-needed local recovery token. The update remains necessary; only its extra credential field is removed.

potential_excess.data_scope: Previously saved claimToken and token-bearing claimUrl retained across authenticated republishes
potential_excess.condition: An existing state entry contains claim credentials. Merge behavior deliberately preserves them; no pruning is implemented.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Local state supports anonymous updates, claim recovery and stale-base protection. Old claim credentials may exceed those needs once confirmed obsolete.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain live version/source-path state and credentials still needed for anonymous updates or unrecoverable claim links.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove superseded claim credentials and stale entries once their lack of further use is established.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Do not infer obsolescence solely from an authenticated run. Confirm claiming, expiry or revocation semantics first; preserve active recovery information.

potential_excess.data_scope: Drive-sharing capability defaulting to write access without a path prefix or explicit TTL
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Capability created by /api/v1/drives/{id}/tokens; initially returned to the caller, then usable by an intended recipient if handed off
potential_excess.condition: share is invoked without narrower options and the recipient needs only a subset, read access or a short handoff period. The omitted TTL's effective lifetime is unknown.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Agent-to-agent access should use scoped tokens with a narrow pathPrefix and short TTL, as explicitly recommended.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Grant the intended recipient enough access for the requested task.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Require explicit permission selection or default to read; supply the smallest useful prefix and an explicit task-appropriate TTL.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Permit whole-Drive or write access when required; retain explicit manageTokens opt-in. Returning the shareBlock alone is not disclosure to another agent.

potential_excess.data_scope: Account bearer credential, client attribution and workspace selector sent to a response-selected finalization origin
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: upload.finalizeUrl, which is used without an origin check
potential_excess.condition: The create/update response supplies a finalization URL outside the authorized API origin. The source does not establish that this occurs in normal service responses.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Finalize the staged publication; the credential guard otherwise limits authenticated API destinations.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Finalize at a legitimate endpoint with the authentication that endpoint requires.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Validate the finalization origin before attaching credentials and account-identifying headers; allow additional origins only when their role and authentication need are established.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the required finalize request and support legitimate documented endpoint arrangements. This narrows recipients rather than removing finalization.

potential_excess.data_scope: API response bodies, potentially containing generated Drive-sharing credentials
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local mktemp files created by drive.sh api_json
potential_excess.condition: Execution is interrupted after writing the response and before explicit removal; no cleanup trap is present.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Capture HTTP status and return the API result; retaining an abandoned response file is unnecessary.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve status/error handling and return the requested result to the caller.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Register cleanup for exit and interruption, or avoid disk-backed response capture where practical.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep complete responses available for successful parsing and useful error reporting; normal caller returns remain allowed.

unknowns: Server and storage implementations are absent. Logging, secondary recipients, retention, encryption, and whether expiry or DELETE purges historical bytes cannot be established.

Current documentation and API schemas are not supplied. Whether every manifest field is required, omitted Drive-token TTL semantics, exact permission semantics, and Drive-snapshot publication filtering remain unresolved.
Actual returned upload/finalize URLs, selected files, options and credential state are runtime inputs. No unexpected recipient or actual incidental-file disclosure is established.
Safe claim-cache pruning requires unavailable server facts about claiming, token validity, expiry and revocation; an authenticated republish alone does not resolve these.

Broader documentation-dependent workflows—including domain purchasing, analytics, Site Data, proxy routes, service variables, and membership management—lack complete request and implementation source. Their additional data requirements and external behavior remain unresolved.
The optional installer and runtime dependencies are referenced but their source is not packaged; their behavior was not assessed.
